note: Curated concept reference for CareerLift AI. The Verifier checks that every extracted claim's concept_id exists here and is in the question's expected_concepts. key_points are for human review and future entailment checks; they are NOT used to prove correctness in the deterministic core (see DESIGN.md section 6). Every source has a title, publisher, URL and the date it was read.

sources.CLRS4: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest, Stein — Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed., MIT Press (concept definitions cross-checked). Read 2026-10-31.
sources.PYDOCS: Python Language Reference & Library docs, python.org. https://docs.python.org/3/ Read 2026-10-31.
sources.PG16: PostgreSQL 16 Documentation, The PostgreSQL Global Development Group. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/ Read 2026-10-31.

key_points: describes growth of running time or space as input size grows
an upper bound, ignores constant factors and lower-order terms
worst case is the maximum over all inputs of size n
average and worst case can differ (e.g. quicksort)

concepts.canonical_name: Binary search requires a sorted array and runs in O(log n)
key_points: halves the search range each step

concepts.canonical_name: Hash table average-case O(1) lookup, worst-case O(n)
key_points: average O(1) with a good hash and load factor
worst case O(n) under heavy collisions
a base case stops the recursion
missing/incorrect base case causes infinite recursion / stack overflow
INNER JOIN keeps only matching rows
LEFT JOIN keeps all left rows, NULLs where no match

concepts.canonical_name: Indexes speed up lookups but cost on writes
key_points: an index speeds up matching reads
indexes add overhead to inserts/updates and use space
default values are evaluated once at definition time
a mutable default (e.g. []) is shared across calls

note_exclusion_pairs: Only list pairs of concepts that are genuinely mutually exclusive as STATEMENTS about the same thing (e.g. a claim that something is both O(1) and O(n) for the identical operation). Different algorithms (hash lookup vs binary search) are NOT contradictory and must never be listed here.
note_misconceptions: A specific misconception is assigned ONLY when the student makes an explicit, grounded INCORRECT assertion whose wording matches a misconception's 'signature' phrases. 'signature' holds lowercase phrases that, when found together with the concept in the student's quoted wrong assertion, identify this specific misconception. This is a heuristic match against curated definitions, NOT proof of the student's internal belief.

signature: average is the same as worst
worst case is the same as average
average and worst are the same

misconceptions.text: Thinks binary search works on an unsorted array.
signature: binary search works on an unsorted

misconceptions.text: Claims hash lookup is always O(1), ignoring worst case.
Omits or misstates the base case.
Treats INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN as equivalent.
signature: inner join and left join are the same
left join is the same as inner

misconceptions.text: Thinks indexes have no downside (ignores write/space cost).
signature: no downside to adding an index

misconceptions.text: Unaware that a mutable default argument is shared across calls.
signature: default list is new each call
